([[Ocoee, Florida]]) | college = [[College of Charleston Cougars men's basketball|College of Charleston]] (2016–2020) | highlights = * 3x First-team All-[[Colonial Athletic Association|CAA]] (2018, 2019, 2020) * [[Colonial Athletic Association Men's Basketball Tournament|CAA Tournament]] MVP ([[2018 CAA Men's Basketball Tournament|2018]]) | medal_templates = }} '''Grant Lucas Riller''' (born February 8, 1997) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[College of Charleston Cougars men's basketball|College of Charleston Cougars]]. ==High school career== Riller played basketball for [[Ocoee High School]] in [[Ocoee, Florida]] under head coach Rob Gordon. He was called up to the [[varsity team]] in ninth grade after initially playing at the [[junior varsity team|junior varsity]] level.{{cite web |last1=Collings |first1=Buddy |title=Riller hits thriller for Ocoee |url=https://www.pressreader.com/usa/orlando-sentinel/20141127/282338268188340 |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |publisher=[[PressReader]] |accessdate=December 2, 2019 |date=November 27, 2014}} As a senior on December 28, 2014, Riller scored a school-record 53 points in a win over [[Leesburg High School (Leesburg, Florida)|Leesburg High School]] in the finals of the Ocoee Great 8 tournament.{{cite web |last1=Jackson |first1=Emilee |title=Ocoee's Riller scores 53, leads boys hoops to tourney title |url=https://www.orangeobserver.com/article/ocoees-riller-scores-53-leads-boys-hoops-tourney-title |website=[[West Orange Times & Observer]] |accessdate=December 2, 2019 |date=December 29, 2014}} He averaged 29.1 points per game in his senior season.{{cite web |last1=Miller |first1=Andrew |title=College of Charleston’s Grant Riller to miss season with knee injury |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/college-of-charleston-s-grant-riller-to-miss-season-with/article_f4be9b5a-d8f4-5e3c-872b-becdaaf4d432.html |website=[[The Post and Courier]] |accessdate=December 2, 2019 |date=November 2, 2015}} Riller was deemed a two-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] and was not rated by [[ESPN]] or [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. On October 4, 2014, he committed to play college basketball for the College of Charleston over offers from [[Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball|Cleveland State]], [[FIU Panthers men's basketball|FIU]], and [[Hofstra Pride men's basketball|Hofstra]].{{cite web |title=Grant Riller |url=https://cofcsports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/grant-riller/4220 |publisher=College of Charleston Athletics |accessdate=December 2, 2019}} ==College career== [[File:MBasketball-vs-College of Charleston.jpg|thumb|left|Riller (right) in November 2017]] Riller suffered a knee injury prior to his freshman season and was forced to redshirt. He was forced to wear a knee brace despite working all summer to get to full strength. In his collegiate debut, Riller scored 21 points against [[The Citadel Bulldogs basketball|The Citadel]]. He averaged 13.1 points per game as a freshman, second-best on the team.{{cite web |last1=Miller |first1=Andrew |title=College of Charleston’s Grant Riller limping his way to success on basketball court |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/college-of-charleston-s-grant-riller-limping-his-way-to/article_3006a778-e801-11e6-9dd7-2f62f0f8a3ea.html |website=[[The Post and Courier]] |accessdate=December 2, 2019 |date=February 3, 2017}} Riller scored 20 points and added four steals in a 83–76 overtime victory over [[Northeastern Huskies men's basketball|Northeastern]] in the [[Colonial Athletic Association]] Tournament. He was named 2018 CAA Tournament Most Outstanding player and joined teammate [[Joe Chealey]] on the All-CAA First Team. Riller averaged 18.7 points per game as a sophomore.{{cite web |last1=Ryzewski|first1=Stephen |title=Ocoee High alum Grant Riller leads College of Charleston to NCAA Tournament berth |url=https://www.orangeobserver.com/article/ocoee-high-alum-grant-riller-leads-college-of-charleston-to-ncaa-tournament-berth-observer-preps |website=[[West Orange Times & Observer]] |accessdate=December 2, 2019 |date=March 8, 2018}} He scored a career-high 43 points in a 99–95 loss to [[Hofstra Pride men's basketball|Hofstra]]. As a junior, Riller averaged 21.9 points and 4.1 assists per game and led the Cougars to a 24–9 record.{{cite news |last1=Miller |first1=Andrew |title=College of Charleston’s Grant Riller is CAA preseason player of year, Cougars 2nd in poll |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/college-of-charleston-s-grant-riller-is-caa-preseason-player/article_07b0bf92-eab6-11e9-8a9f-330e1f78db23.html |accessdate=December 2, 2019 |work=[[The Post and Courier]] |date=October 9, 2019}} He was again named first-team All-CAA.{{cite press release|url=https://caasports.com/news/2019/3/8/hofstras-wright-foreman-repeats-as-caa-mens-basketball-player-of-the-year.aspx |title=Hofstra's Wright-Foreman repeats as CAA men's basketball Player of the Year |publisher=[[Colonial Athletic Association]] |date=March 8, 2019 |accessdate=March 8, 2019}} Coming into his senior year, Riller was named CAA preseason player of the year. On December 14, 2019, Riller became the third Cougar in program history to reach the 2,000 career point mark, scoring 21 in a road loss to [[Richmond Spiders men's basketball|Richmond]].{{cite news|last=|first=|url= https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/riller-joins-college-of-charleston-s--career-point-club/article_c2b33a4c-1ed5-11ea-aa97-071037016df9.html |title= Riller joins College of Charleston’s 2,000-career point club in loss to Richmond |publisher=[[The Post and Courier]] |date=December 14, 2019 |accessdate=December 15, 2019}} On January 16, 2020, he recorded the first-ever
